fix: 'stipules evident as N prickles' counts the prickles that the stipules have become, not the stipules. When 'evident as' or 'reduced to' comes before a count, the count belongs to the modified part (spine stipule).
reason: The 3–5 slender prickles around the leaf scar are what the stipules have turned into. The flora does not say there are 3–5 stipules.

fix: 'apex X' after a petal description should move the bearer to the petal apex, as is already done for leaf blades (leaf lamina tip). The swap seems to happen only for leaf blades.
reason: 'apex subrounded' describes the tip of the petal. PO has petal apex (PO_0025144). Obtuse with 'approximately' is fine for 'subrounded'.
In 'Herbs 3-5 × 5-10 dm' the first range is height: 3–5 dm = 30–50 cm. The second range is width and is correctly left out.
The style has 3 stigmas.
PO has no exostome class. Peristome (PO_0030042) is the nearest part that contains it, and the colour dark brown is right.
The leaf blade apex is rounded. The bearer was correctly moved to leaf lamina tip, and the project maps 'rounded' to obtuse.
Leaves alternate.
'basal pinnae slightly shortened, up to 7 cm': the 7 cm belongs to the basal pinnae, which fits the third pinnae being up to 10 cm. Pinna = leaflet, with the basal context noted.

fix: 'lateral veins' (and 'nerves'/'veins' with 'on each side') should map to secondary leaf vein inside the leaf blade, not to the anatomical vascular bundle. Note too that 'about 5' should carry the 'approximately' qualifier.
reason: The flora counts the leaf's lateral (secondary) veins, about 5 on each side of the midrib.
Rhizome prostrate.
'Shrubs or small trees' gives two habit values: shrub habit (frutescent) or tree habit (arborescent).
5–9 teeth on each side of the leaf (or leaflet) blade. The leaf as the containing part is acceptable here.
Anthers pale yellow.

fix: 'n-seriate' / '-sériées' gives the number of rows (series), not the number of parts. Read it as an arrangement (multiseriate, biseriate, uniseriate) with the number of series. Do not read it as an amount of the part (pattern 03 says 'seriate' is not split).
reason: The involucral bracts are in 4–5 rows. The flora does not say there are 4–5 bracts.
Branches subjulaceous = approximately julaceous. Julaceous (FLOPO_0991232) is allowed on branches.
The cymes (inflorescences) are pubescent.
(0.3-)0.4-1.9(-2.2) dm = 4–19 cm, with extremes of 3 and 22 cm, converted correctly.
Achenes yellowish = approximately yellow.
The stem leaves are 2–2.8 mm long. 'Leaf' is acceptable for a moss stem leaf.

fix: In Apiaceae (and in 'umbels ... rays N'), 'rays' are the main branches of a compound umbel, not ray flowers. When 'rays' follows 'umbel(s)' or comes with lengths in cm, map it to the inflorescence branch. 'Subequal' here also means equal in length.
reason: These rays are 2–3 cm stalks of a compound umbel, not ray flowers.
'Blade not arcuate' = the blade is not curved, so negated curvature on the leaf blade is right. There is no specific 'arcuate' term to use.

target: from_value: lanceolate shape tending to oblong (no oblong-lanceolate term), not oblong (PATO_0000946)
fix: A hyphenated shape 'X-Y' is a shape Y tending to X: the head is the last part. Reading 'oblong-lanceolate' as oblong drops the main shape. Map it to the last word (or a compound term), never to the first word alone.
reason: 'Oblong-lanceolate to lanceolate' is a range within lanceolate shapes. The record makes it run from oblong to lanceolate.
The calyx is inflated in fruit and up to 3.5 cm long. The 'in fruit' stage is attached.
Inflorescence terminal or axillary.
'Basally attached' = basifixed. Bracts are an allowed bearer.
14–19 secondary veins on each side of the midvein, in the leaf blade.
The older stems are spirally twisted. The 'old' context (PATO_0000308) is attached.
The lateral united petals are not clawed: clawed is negated on the petal.

fix: 'apex X to Y' after a leaf-blade description should move the bearer to the leaf lamina tip, as is done for 'apex X' (compare A00455). The move is skipped when the apex word is inside a qualitative 'to' range (from_text 'apex acuminate').
reason: Acuminate to acute describes the blade apex, not the whole blade.
Twigs subangular = young stems approximately angular.
